_comment: Skill pairs that score as near-duplicates but are legitimately distinct.
Add a pair here ONLY after reading both descriptions and confirming a real
difference in scope, platform, or offense-vs-defense posture. The 'reason'
is not bookkeeping: it is the wording each skill's negative trigger should
use, e.g. reason 'Linux vs Windows' becomes 'Do not use for Windows hosts
A pair that is genuinely ambiguous does NOT belong here. Disambiguate the
Regenerate the candidate list with: python tools/detect-collisions.py

reviewed_distinct.reason: Same CIS Benchmark methodology, different operating systems. The controls, tooling and audit commands do not overlap, so both must exist; each description must name the OS explicitly and point at the other.
Passive IDS monitoring/inspection and SIEM log integration vs inline IPS (NFQueue) that actively blocks traffic. Each must name the mode and point at the other.

Security review of existing functions to find risks (permissive roles, injection, missing protections) vs hardening/deploying functions (least privilege, dependency scanning, secrets, runtime monitoring). Assess vs remediate.
Static analysis of a captured trojanized artifact (malware-analysis) vs proactive SIEM/EDR threat hunt for T1195 compromise (threat-hunting). Offense artifact vs defensive hunt.
Investigating a specific incident through log correlation in Splunk ES vs authoring reusable SPL detection/correlation rules for a SOC. Analyst vs detection engineer.

Embedding AFL++ fuzzing into a CI/CD pipeline (harness/instrumentation/persistent mode) vs standalone coverage-guided fuzzing of a binary (afl-cmin/cmin, crash triage). CI integration vs ad-hoc campaign.
Extract a beacon configuration from a captured PE/memory dump vs parse a Malleable C2 profile (AST) to produce network detection signatures. Artifact config vs profile grammar.
